item.title: First thoughts after watching Classroom of the Elite Season 4 Episode 16
item.description:
I am a light novel reader for this series and this note includes a spoiler.

I watched Classroom of the Elite, COTE, season 4, episode 16, which was the final episode in this season. It was a great episode with a lot of fighting scenes and worth watching as anime.

At first, Horikita found the note that Kiyotaka Ayanokoji will be expelled in I-2, and decided to go there. She met Ibuki and then Amasawa in the middle of the way. And Ibuki left in order to get more points than Horikita. Afterward, Horikita started talking to Amasawa, and Amasawa was just trying to provoke her about not knowing Ayanokoji well enough and tried to block her. She felt it was going to fight so she prepared to fight and Amasawa started. Obviously, Horikita couldn't win against Amasawa; she was thrown with Judo, and then Amasawa kicked her and knocked her down. But Amasawa's goal was to buy her time. Afterward, she stood up and Amasawa tried to punch Ibuki, but Ibuki caught her fist. Well, it's a little weird to me that Amasawa couldn't see Ibuki even though she was in front of her. Anyhow, they started fighting against Amasawa together. Time by time they argued with each other about a few things, and each time, Amasawa just watched them without attacking. It was good because obviously, her purpose wasn't to win against them, or at least she underestimated them. Then Horikita learned something from Amasawa and told Ibuki about it, and then Amasawa suddenly froze and took a hit from both of them. Then Horikita and Ibuki found out she had taken damage on the side of her belly. And Amasawa allowed them to pass by, because she had earned enough time. If that hit had come from Tsukishiro, it would defeat her purpose of being able to stop anyone who was trying to reach the place. Or maybe she didn't do what she was told and he didn't care. In terms of animation, Amasawa's fighting was so smooth as she moved against 2 people, and it was patently obvious she was so agile and powerful in that fight.

Second, Ayanokoji fought against Tsukishiro and another teacher. I forgot who he was. He fought against them and tried to avoid their attacks, standing at a place where a wave of the sea reached his foot on the beach. Were they that strong? He couldn't attack them at all, or he was still just trying to learn how they were attacking. But then, Kiryuin came and joined them without knowing why they were fighting. She was the person who just moved by her curiosity, and the 1st year students tried to kick Ayanokoji out, which made her curious, so she stalked him. She also talked as if she is a lady, but exceptionally, she had fighting or martial arts experience. As a result, Ayanokoji fought against Tsukishiro alone. The fighting scene was, unlike Amasawa and Horikita and Ibuki, unrealistic, and Ayanokoji's movement was like an MC with superpowers. Tsukishiro was strong, and also wicked enough that he had an ace up his sleeve. So he tried to create an opening using sand and attacked, but of course, Ayanokoji figured it out and stopped him by pinning his fingers to Tsukishiro's neck. Then other teachers came and Tsukishiro couldn't fight anymore and he failed. Also, Horikita and Ibuki came and ended there.

spoiler comments of light novels. Well, what's so weird was Horikita didn't figure out anything from this scene in the light novel even after this. That was definitely weird that someone tried to get Ayanokoji expelled and there were only teachers there. She should've been suspicious, especially since she's a smart enough character to be a leader in a class. Also, Kiryuin suddenly came up before this island exam, and came to this very important fighting scene. But if I remember correctly, this was the only scene she was mainly involved with Ayanokoji. She was brought in probably because the author needed a character who moved by her curiosity only, didn't tell secrets to others nor ask anything, and then fought so that Ayanokoji was able to focus on fighting against Tsukishiro. It would've been weird if Tsukishiro had fought against him by himself even though he knew Ayanokoji was a masterpiece in the Whiteroom.
Amasawa disobeyed orders from Tsukishiro a lot, so she couldn't go back to the Whiteroom anymore and she was okay to stay or leave the school. Well, if disobeying many times causes expulsion from the Whiteroom, why not the same for Ayanokoji? Maybe Amasawa wasn't that good there.

Afterward, the exam's results were announced. All of the bottom 5 were from the 3rd year grade, instead of the 1st or 2nd year grades, and Nagumo didn't save them. Well, why were they so bad? Even though they needed to follow Nagumo, some of the 1st years or 2nd years were worse than them. Or simply because the 1st and 2nd year leaders were way better than the 3rd years. Then 3rd place was Sakayanagi, 2nd was Nagumo, and 1st was Koenji. Nagumo was trying to collect the points to that group, so that was the reason why their points were way better than any of the 2nd year or 1st year groups. Still, Sakayanagi's group was good enough to beat other groups despite the fact that she couldn't move. Well, in the ship, Karuizawa thought about the kiss with Ayanokoji and she was like a main heroine here. Also, Ryuen and Sakayanagi talked about some kinds of deals, and Sakayanagi and Ayanokoji talked about similar things. These are the setup for season 5. Horikita just told Ayanokoji that they reached class C and are close to class B now.

Anyway, this is the end of season 4. The island exam was long, and there were a lot of fighting scenes. The animation was good for anyone, like Koenji, Ryuen, Housen, Ayanokoji, and Amasawa. Also, the animation of the island was good enough that we could see how they did it, unlike in the novel where we could just imagine it. Maybe the scene between Ayanokoji and Ichinose was a little over-romanticized, though. And also the leaders battle between Tsubaki and Sakayanagi was a good one. I remember in the light novel, Tsubaki figured out Sakayanagi was behind the scenes, but that scene was cut somehow. Let's wait and see in season 5.

Watched the 2nd time.

I overlooked many things. First, the memo left for Horikita was written by an honest person, because it's not even a code, so everyone can understand what it means. So, very likely Ichinose. But Ichinose didn't show her smile on the ship when she found out something. Maybe there was no scene where she saw him; well, but it was a kind of important scene, so it's going to be included in season 5, I guess.

Second, I overlooked that Amasawa clearly said Horikita was able to take a rest for 5 or 10 minutes while they were fighting.

Also, I didn't notice that when Kiryuin appeared, the BGM changed to hers. This is the kind of character who has her own BGM, which happens in some anime. She might be a favorite character of the production company.

Also, when Horikita came to the beach, Tsukishiro and Shiba had already left, so she couldn't find out and figure out what happened. Ayanokoji's tornado movement to avoid attacks from both Tsukishiro and Shiba, and also doing a front flip, was amazing and unreal.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Classroom of the Elite Season 4 Episode 14
item.description:
I am a light novel reader for this series and this note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Classroom of the Elite, COTE, season 4, episode 14. It started not from Ayanokoji, but from Kiriyama's PoV. Koenji was 2nd place, close to the Nagumo's group, and Kiriyama was sure that Nagumo and he were the only people who could stop Koenji. So 10 or more people in the 3rd years students were trying to follow, negotiate, and get them in the middle of Koenji's way. I don't remember exactly how many details the LN included, but I felt it's not as detailed as anime, so animators really liked Koenji. He was extraordinary, for sure. He can climb up a cliff just by jumps, he slept but only for a short amount of time, because his REM sleep cycle was, what was that? shorter than others? And then, he wasn't scared on the narrow cliff pathway at all while others did. In the first place, the island isn't really a good place for an exam considering how dangerous it is.

Kiriyama couldn't control the group and his group started attacking to Koenji. They wanted to get a reward of A-class's ticket from Nagumo, so they needed an achievement. But they were easily defeated. Koenji definitely attacked some people, but for some people, didn't he just push them? But they couldn't stand up after his attack and he left the place. Kiriyama planned something because he assumed Koenji thought 3rd year students couldn't do anything to him later. I don't remember he was a smart character, though.

By the way, except Koenji, the only 2nd-year group that entered the top 10 was Sakayanagi's, with Ichinose, and they were just rank 10, so they weren't actually that good compared to the 3rd years students. Maybe there is a spoiler here for the 3rd year students so I don't say the details. But still, was Nagumo's ability that much higher compared to all of 2nd years leaders? I didn't feel so after reading all volumes of the 2nd year's LNs.

On the other hand, Ayanokoji met some students from class B, Shiina and Ishizaki and worked together. At a night, Nanase somehow figured out his place and came to his tent and then shared 1st years' plan.

3 days ago, she met with Housen and another student happened to come to him and then gave him the transceiver. That was from Utomiya, and they argued before reaching to the conclusion. Housen somehow knew Tsubaki was near him and she persuaded him to expel a few students who work alone like Ayanokoji and that's what Housen wanted. Tsubaki understood the essence of characters pretty well and gave them what they want, and she also achieved what she wanted. She also noticed somehow Nanase was around Housen. This woman was actually a lot like Ayanokoji.

Then Yagami came to Utomiya and Tsubaki and gave them the information about the place of Ayanokoji. But Tsubaki knew it beforehand so Yagami couldn't get any reward of expelling Ayanokoji. Utomiya also was suspicious to Yagami because he broke his wristband twice already though Utomiya himself did it only once. Probably that once was deliberate one so he was suspicious to Yagami. Then Yagami left that scene, and Tsubaki using transceivers to surround Ayanokoji. By looking at these, at least Tsubaki seemed to be really from the White room for sure. And what did Yagami do here?

On the other hand, Ayanokoji used a GPS feature and he identified the locations of Yagami, Utomiya, and Tsubaki somehow and noticed 1st years students are surrounded. He didn't even think they were dangerous enough to change his plan. In the 1st place, how did he know where each student was, even though he didn't meet any of them, by just using a GPS search? Did he know enough about 1st years students at that point? Especially, Tsubaki, Utomiya, and Yagami didn't do anything before the exam.

Anyway, everybody knows something big will happen in the next episode.

Watched again. Mikitani and others were really mob enemies who are willing to violent as usual and were easily be defeated. A woman in the class B said Ayanokoji was harmless and I know that's how most students thought he was, but I really felt they were terribly dense from the watcher's view. What happened between Tsubaki and Utomiya? I think even til the end of 2nd years' volumes, they didn't talk anything. And until here, this show really showed that she was suspicious as the one from the White room, considering how badly she wanted to expel, and she didn't care if she was expelled.

Well, but animators really enjoyed animating Koenji. They did whatever they want for him to make him stronger and more agile.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero season 4 episode 11
item.description:
I watched the Re:Zero season 4 episode 11. I remember the story for season 2 and 3 only a little, but don't remember the details of each character that much. This note includes a spoiler.

So, in the previous episode, Ram figured out Subaru was not who he used to be. He was trying to attack her to hide it, but Emilia was there too, and she put him into an ice cage in the same room. Then he confessed he lost his memory. Ram didn't believe him, or was even angry with him. It's because he was the only one who remembers Rem, so if nobody remembered her sister, she was upset. And she tried to attack him, but Emilia was trying to save him. Ram pushed her to the side and attacked him, then he shut out his mind, so he became another Subaru. The question I had was Ram said something about Rem, and asked him about what happened to Rem. I felt it was something wrong to Rem in the spirit room, but I couldn't figure out what it was.

Anyway, then Subaru got back himself, and then saw "Subaru was here" everywhere in the room's wall. How did he do it? No clue. But then Reid came to the room. Reid was somehow out of the 2nd floor, and I wondered about it, but something was changed. I guess, Emilia went to the exam on the 1st floor and did something, probably passed it. That's why Reid didn't have to be there and came out of it. But I thought he was dead and he couldn't come out or he would disappear, but he didn't?! Will there be 2 Sword saints, then? Anyway, then Reid and Subaru walked around the tower and they found Julius. Somehow, he was downstairs and fought against mabeasts alone. What happened? Maybe he was a decoy to escape others. He was about to be dead, so Subaru was thinking about reading Julius's death book afterward, but Julius shouted to warn him. And then Reid came to downstairs and defeat those mabeasts. Anyway, Reid wanted to fight Julius, so they started fighting. Julius relied on Subaru to protect Foxidna and Anastasia. And Subaru decided to run to find them.

He then found Baeko and Foxidna. Foxidna warned Baeko that he was fake according to Ram. Then he told he lost his memory but she didn't believe him. Baeko looked really surprised and was sad, so she really was a kid reaction and adorable. But then Subaru cried out how the hell he wanted to be him because he didn't like himself. They were really surprised about how he felt, but Baeko still trusted him. Foxidna anyway stayed away from him, but he was trusted about her by Julius, so he pulled her and moved together. Then mabeasts attacked and they defeated them, but then, those deadbodies exploded. Baeko was gone, and then Subaru pulled Foxidna, but she lost her lower body and about to be dead. He was trying to put her out of her misery, but he couldn't, and at that time, finally, Foxidna admitted he was him. She said it was good that Anastasia didn't have to experience that pains and she did instead, so what she said before that she would lose her life if it can save Anastasia was really true.

Then the Witch came. She repeated I love you to Subaru, and he was about to be completely in her mana, but right before that, Emilia saved him. And instantly, she was gone and Emilia pulled him and started running. But then, he cried out and didn't understand why people still wanted to work with him. So, while the Witch's mana came to them, Emilia shared what happened since she met him from the first time. And then confessed she loved him, and he noticed original him did his best to save her. It totally made sense that everyone's trust put him pressure because he didn't like himself. What was sad to me was, the Mathers' villages' incident didn't include Rem, because Emilia didn't remember her, so it was only by Subaru and Ram. Also, from Emilia's perspective, he didn't mess up a lot so impressions of what Subaru actually did and felt lost from what she shared. Then the ground was collapsed somehow and Emilia and Subaru went to the... mana? Then Subaru pulled himself together again right before going into that. Then next time, he woke up right after he came to the another world at the first time in his memory.

Overall these episodes were great. It was interesting to see what happened to a loops' main character if they don't remember a thing, and these episodes exactly show that. In the end, it seems Subaru pulled himself together and passed exams. That said, these are 3rd times that Subaru needed to go through painful experiences. 1st time was when he was saved by Rem when he confronted the White whale and Petelgeus, and 2nd time was when Otto saved him at the graveyard and needed to resolve the exam there and the Mather's mansion. Plus, Emilia will lose these memories so how much will this be important? Well, if he doesn't remember his past, this experience is probably the most important experience to him, though. That might be a thing to make Emilia as the most important main character to him. Before that, Rem was also one of the most important person still to him.

Also, I thought the Witch appeared in the tower again. I thought the Witch overtook Emilia's body at the graveyard and in the tower, but she came to rescue Subaru. So, who was the Witch? This character might be unrelated to existing characters, but in some stories, these characters might be actually from known characters. For example, Foxidna might be actually Echidna of the Witch and will take over Anastasia in the future. Assuming that, she appeared at the graveyard and in the tower, and only possible characters who could be was Emilia or Ram in both places. Ram is very unlikely, though. I mean, even if she could, how could she repeat to Subaru that she loves him indefinitely? So, Emilia, then? At the graveyard, she lost her mental and I thought that was the cause which made her the Witch. Seems unlikely here, so what happened?

Anyway, this is the end of the part of the season 4, and there has been nothing to be solved. These are something Subaru has to figure it out. First, who killed Subaru in the tower? Perhaps, Meili, from the feeling that she didn't want others to know that she was in the archive. Second, why did Subaru lose his memory? I guess he read a gospel and that took over his body. Third, how to pass the exam with the 2nd floor? Well, this will be that they are going to read books in the archive and find a solution for sure. Fourth, what did Ram find about Rem? Still no idea. Fifth, what happened to Rem, or someone looks like Rem when she killed Subaru in the 3rd life? Most likely she was one of the Sin Archbishop, but where was she from? Meili called her somehow?

So, let's wait for the following part in months.

Watched 2nd time.

I misunderstood that something happened to Rem but she didn't mention anything in this episode, apparently. Still, there was an animation that she noticed something in the previous episode about her, so what was that?

It was also painful to watch the end of Foxidna in the episode. The last word was to apologize to Subaru for him, rather than something for Anastasia or Julius at all.

Also, Shaula and Ram didn't show up after he lost his memory after he was trapped into an ice cage. It seemed that some monsters were going around in the tower when Shaula was gone, so something happened to her? Maybe Emilia and others couldn't solve exams appropriately. Ram wasn't there because, I don't know. Was she killed by somehow? And then the woman when she came in the 3rd loop didn't appear at all in the fourth loop.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero season 4 episode 10
item.description:
I watched the Re:Zero season 4 episode 10. I remember the story for season 2 and 3 only a little, but don't remember the details of each character that much. This note includes a spoiler.

Subaru was surprised that Meili was dead on the floor and he obviously killed her, but he didn't remember what happened. So he hid her under a podium and left the room. Then Emilia came to him and worried about him and he wondered how kind she was to him. He was basically shut-in who couldn't do anything before coming to the world, so no wonder. Then Ram came to them, and she asked them to go to the archive where Baeko was there.

Baeko found out the dead book of Meili. They discussed who would read it, and Baeko suggested it should be either Subaru or Julius. And, why? They didn't have mana that much? Subaru may not be necessary for Reid but Julius should, so I don't get why she suggested them, instead of Ram or Emilia. Emilia was hesitant to read the book but Shaula suggested reading it, as if she doesn't care people's deaths. Probably she killed people so many so far, lives are nothing special for her, obviously. Then as suggested, Subaru read the book.

The book was of course about Meili's life. She was picked up by a wolf. It's weird that the wolf didn't eat her but well, it's a fantasy. Then Elsa came and she kills her parents, wolves, and Elsa picked up Meili. She was brought to her mother, who was the Sin Archbishop who can change their forms in the season 3. I forgot her name nor which one her sin was. Anyway, she traveled around with Elsa, and she killed people without any hesitation anywhere, and she was surprised and frightened. Well, naturally, because it might've been her turn next. But then Elsa was gone, and actually, she still didn't learn how to show emotions. She was just trying to immitate Elsa until then. Then Subaru found her, and brought her to the tower. So, for her, the village's issue wasn't the serious nor important thing she wanted to remember. She wanted to find something in the archive, but Subaru found her and she avoided him. Who's book she wanted to find? Elsa? Anyway, then somehow she didn't want to be found by anyone and be known, so wanted to do something against him. And next time, he was in the archive, and was reading books. But then he said something to her. It was obviously not Subaru. Did he find and read a gospel and became one of Sin Archbishops? Then next day, she talked about what he said while he was the Archbishop, and the that man killed her. So, that means, before he lost the memory, he became that man, and even after he lost his memory, he still was that man.

After reading the Meili's book, he was so shocked, confused, and couldn't talk. Because he was so afraid of being found that he killed her, he saw an illusion of her and heard her voice from her illusion. Everyone avoided reading the book because he was unable to react and respond, except that Shaula seemed to know what he did. And then, they couldn't find her body, and they decided not to find it anymore.

Then Ram came to the place, and found out Subaru wasn't him. Then he was so on the edge, he almost made up his mind to kill her to hide it. Because the illusion he was seeing said to him that murder became a habit to solve another problem once that person had succeeded to do so. But this is the end of the episode.

The body lost because I guess Ram knew he killed and the body was there, because she called him and Emilia, and didn't want others to look it. Maybe Foxidna also knew it. Other people couldn't hide anything with straight faces so these were only people who were suspicious, other than Shaula. Obviously, Ram has an ability to look someone through the Mabeast, so used it to Patrasche and followed him, and showed Subaru the same gesture as he had done to Patrasche against him.

Well, it was fun, but nothing is clear yet, and the next episode is the final episode in the season 4, or at least in the part of this season. Do I need to wait for a long time for what will happen? Really?

Did Subaru become the other Sin Archbishop like when he did during Petelgeus? It seemed not, but I couldn't say for sure. I noticed why Subaru started questioning about himself, because from his perspective, Subaru with his own memory was the person who was murder of Meili and seemed to do the same thing against other people like Emilia or Baeko. So in the later episode, what the illusion Subaru saw looks like Meili said and behaved basically the Subaru's inner thought and just talked to him. Also, Subaru was so afraid of being found out, cameras often pointed out necks who he targeted.

In terms of why/how the Meili body wasn't found, I bet Shaula hid it. Shaula noticed Subaru did something to Meili somehow, so that's why. Why did she notice about it was unclear, though. She hadn't known the archive before Subaru came, so she didn't know the dead book must include the moment when a person is dead or not. She may be able to figure out who is lying or not?

Another unclear thing was, when Ram was trying to find Meili, she came to the spirit room, saw Rem's body, and found out about something. What was that about? Was there anything suspicious? No idea.

Then thinking back who killed Subaru in the 1st or 2nd loop in the tower, I guess it was likely Meili. Ram could be if she could've found out Subaru could be the Sin ArchBishop, but she didn't and also asked questions to him and wanted him not to lose the memory. Meili could have done it because, in this memory, she said she didn't want to be seen in the archive but he saw her, so she pushed him to avoid being noticed. Subaru allowed do whatever she wanted, and that might be the one she wanted? No, not pretty make sense, but could be

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero season 4 episode 9
item.description:
I watched the Re:Zero season 4 episode 9. I remember the story for season 2 and 3 only a little, but don't remember the details of each character that much. This note includes a spoiler.

This episode was the best one in the season 4. So we figured out who was the main heroine. Patrasche. Period.

Subaru went outside of the tower, and faced a sand worm. I think this was owned by Meili. Right before he was eaten, it was killed by Shaula's magics. I thought she would attack him next, but instead, he fell down into the quicksand. He didn't even see her at all.

Then he went to the underground again, and walked to the right side of the crosswalk, and hit the 3rd wall. He couldn't open the gate, but somehow, the gate lit up and he was moved to the watchtower. Why? There was no hint so no idea. Maybe because he was the only one and he was the master of Shaula?

It seemed he went nuts again, or maybe he went to pieces because of the pressure that he would be killed by others, so he talked himself to persuade him to kill others. That was exactly what happened to him when he faced to Petelgeus. He thought he was able to kill someone who had killed him no matter who, though he had no ability to do so, and he knew it, so he was kinda. arrogant?

Then when he went to the upstairs, the first thing he saw was Shaula's dead body. So, because he pretended to be strong, he was frightened about that and thought she wasn't the one. I was anticipating some ugly mabeast from Shaula would come and kill him. Actually, the subtitle of this episode is Empty shell, so it was perhaps about her in this scene.

Then he looked around and found many dead bodies. Ram was dead in front of the chair which Rem sit and which Ram pushed, and she had something on her back, or maybe her back was cut through.
